types.ExitArgs: What an `exitStep` caller names: `cancels`, resting orders to cancel (each a `Cancel`: its asset id, whether `id` is a client id, and the id); `perps`, DEX 0 perps holding a position besides the strategy's own; `dexes`, HIP-3 DEXes to watch (each a `DexHint`: the DEX's index and the collateral token its balance is moved to spot in, USDC 0 or a pinned stablecoin, anything else read as USDC). A wrong hint is refused by Hyperliquid and costs nothing.
types.Holding: One holding in a leg's report: an asset id (`keccak256("dltx.asset.USD")`, `keccak256("dltx.asset.ETH")`) and a signed quantity in 18 decimals.
types.StrategyConfig: A strategy's whole configuration, which the owner signs to create it, field by field (amendment 2d: `CreateVault`, below): the combination factory, the execution group whose key operates it, the hub's chain and parameters (`HubParams`, encoded), and its 2 to 4 legs. The hub is member 0, the legs members 1 onwards.
types.LegConfig: One leg of a strategy: its leg code, its chain (a CCTP domain number), its role (long or short), and the leg type's own parameters, encoded (for the long contract its pinned protocols, health floor, price bound, daily loss budget and fast-bridge fee cap; for the short contract its market, order bound, fast-bridge fee cap and fee budget).
types.LegPin: What a combination factory pins for each leg of its pairing: the leg code, the hash its code must have, its chain, its role, how the hub knows its value (read on its own chain, or reported), and the leg type's parameters as a typed-data struct: its name, its fields and how many (amendment 2d), as the leg code's `paramsType()` declares them.
types.PriceSourcePin: A price the hub values a strategy with, pinned by the combination factory for one hub chain and one asset: a Chainlink feed in USD, or a rate and its base's USD feed, and the oldest round accepted, in seconds.
types.SequencerPin: The sequencer uptime feed of one layer-2 hub chain: while the sequencer is down, or just back, the hub values nothing.
types.Cancel: A resting Hyperliquid order to cancel in an exit: its market, and its order id or the client id it was placed with.
types.DexHint: A Hyperliquid market (DEX) for the exit to read, and the collateral token its balance is sent back in (USDC or a pinned stablecoin). A wrong hint is refused by Hyperliquid and costs nothing.

exitModule.does: The fixed module this contract's code runs some of its functions in, by DELEGATECALL in this contract's own storage. On the hub it is the fee module (`StrategyHubFee`); on the long contract, `LongVaultExit`; on the short contract, `ShortVaultExit`. It is set in the code's constructor with its code hash checked, and can never change.

fallback.does: Runs one of the module's functions in this contract's storage, and refuses every other call. On the hub: `snapshot`, `crystallize`, `payout`, `setFeeRate`, `value` and `preview`. On the long contract: `exitStep`, `exitPart`, `receiveMint`, `report`, `holdings`, `claimRewards`, `claimMerkl`, `swapReward`, `rewardCollateralOff` and `rewardPins`. On the short contract: `exitStep`, `bridgeOut`, `ownerOrder`, `proposeSweep`, `sweepResidue`, `exitStatus`, `receiveMint`, `report` and `holdings`.
fallback.who: Anyone may call; each function it runs applies its own rule on who may call it.
checks: The call's function selector is one of the module's functions listed for this contract; anything else reverts (`Unsupported`).

checks: Not already initialised. The member code itself can never be initialised: its `factory` is set at deployment.
One to four links, with exactly one domain per link, and no link at the zero address.
Its own parameters, as the contract type reads them. On the hub, the factory must also give one value kind per leg.

Each `READY` to another chain is tried with a fixed gas allowance. If less gas is left than that try needs, the whole call reverts (`GasTooLow`), so a low gas estimate can never skip a message. If Circle refuses the message, `ReadyPending` records it and `announceReady` sends it again.

receiveLocal.does: Takes `amount` of USDC from another member on this chain, which allowed exactly that amount just before, and counts it in `receivedFrom`. On the hub, it is booked as a move between members, never as new capital.
receiveLocal.who: Another member of the strategy on the same chain, from inside its own transfer to this contract.
receiveLocal.when: In every state, the exit included.
checks: The caller is one of this contract's links, and that link is on this chain.

pause.when: Outside the exit, while the owner has not revoked the execution key on this contract.
checks: The contract is not in its exit.

ownerAction.does: Carries out one action the owner signed for this contract. Action 1 revokes the execution key here; action 2 allows it again. On the short contract only, action 3 replaces the Hyperliquid agent, action 4 cancels any pending agent and action 5 releases the exit's reservation of USDC sent from spot (budget mode). Revoking on the short contract also drops DLTX's pending agent proposal.
ownerAction.who: The owner: a local action signed by one credential in effect in the deposit contract on this chain. Anyone may submit it.
ownerAction.when: In any state, before the signature's deadline. Each contract is revoked and allowed on its own: revoking one does not revoke the others.
checks: The deadline has not passed.

The signature is the owner's `VaultAction(address vault, uint256 chainId, uint8 action, address agent, uint256 nonce, uint256 deadline)`, naming this contract, this chain and the signing credential's current nonce (`ownerNonceOf(credential)`). Each credential has its own nonce: its signatures are accepted once, in order (an older "allow" cannot be replayed after the same credential's "revoke"), and no other credential can spend it, so none can block another's action by acting first.
The credential named is the one that made the signature: a wallet's recovered address, a passkey's key, as the deposit contract reads them; anything else reverts (`BadSignature`).
On the hub and the long contract, actions 3, 4 and 5 revert (`Unsupported`), and the nonce is not used up.
On the short contract, action 3 with the burner (`burner()`) takes effect at once. Any other agent waits 24 hours (`applyOwnerAgent`), and a zero agent reverts.

On the short contract, action 5 sets the reservation (`reserved`) to zero: the owner's word that the USDC sends from spot to HyperEVM it counts will not execute. What was reserved may then leave spot again.

params.action: 1 revoke the execution key, 2 allow it again, 3 replace the agent (the short contract only), 4 cancel the pending agents (the short contract only), 5 release the exit's reservation (the short contract only).
params.agent: For action 3, the new agent. The other actions ignore it, but it is signed all the same.
params.credential: The signing credential's id in the deposit contract (`credentialId`: keccak of its kind, x and y), whose nonce the signature carries.
params.deadline: When the signature expires, as a Unix time in seconds: the call reverts after it.
params.signature: One owner credential's signature over the EIP-712 message, in the deposit contract's "DLTX Owner" domain (no chain id): `0x01 ‖ r ‖ s ‖ v` for a wallet, or `0x02 ‖ x ‖ y ‖` the ABI-encoded WebAuthn assertion for a passkey.

beginExit.does: Puts this contract in its exit for good, then tells every other member of the strategy: a direct `legExit()` call on this chain, a Circle message at fast finality to another chain. A member it cannot tell is recorded in `toldPending` for `notifyLink`, and the exit here stands. On entering, the short contract replaces its agent with the burner, and the hub fixes the exit's fee base at its high-water mark.
beginExit.who: The owner: a `BeginExit(strategyId, deadline)` signed by one credential in effect in the deposit contract on this chain. Anyone may submit it.
beginExit.when: In any state. The signature has no nonce and names the strategy, not a contract or a chain, so one signature works on every member. On a contract already in its exit it changes nothing.
checks: The deadline has not passed.
One owner credential in effect on this chain signed it. On HyperEVM the deposit contract's copy must have received the owner record first.
Each Circle message is tried with a fixed gas allowance. If less gas is left than that try needs, the whole call reverts (`GasTooLow`), so a low gas estimate can never skip a member.

params.signature: One owner credential's signature over `BeginExit`, in the deposit contract's "DLTX Owner" domain (no chain id): `0x01 ‖ r ‖ s ‖ v` for a wallet, or `0x02 ‖ x ‖ y ‖` the ABI-encoded WebAuthn assertion for a passkey.

beginExitStopped.does: The escape hatch: puts this contract in its exit for good once DLTX has stopped checking in, then tells every other member, as `beginExit` does.
beginExitStopped.when: Once this chain's registry reports the group stopped: 7 days without a check-in, or a group that was never given a key. On a contract already in its exit it changes nothing.

notifyLink.does: Tells member `k` that this contract is in its exit, when the first try failed: a direct `legExit()` call on this chain, or a Circle message at fast finality to another chain.
notifyLink.when: In the exit, while `k` is still marked in `toldPending`. Retry until it succeeds.
checks: This contract is in its exit and has not yet told member `k`.
It reverts if Circle refuses the message, or if a member on this chain has no code yet, so the mark stays until the member is told.

legExit.does: Another member on this chain says it is in its exit. This contract stops waiting to tell that member, and enters its own exit if it has not already. A contract told by another member tells nobody else.
legExit.who: Another member of the strategy on the same chain, while it enters its exit or retries telling.
legExit.when: In any state. On a contract already in its exit, it only clears the caller's mark in `toldPending`.
checks: The caller is one of this contract's links, and that link is on this chain.

handleReceiveFinalizedMessage.does: Receives a message from another member on another chain. `READY` marks that member ready; an exit message puts this contract in its exit for good, telling nobody else; a report is stored by the hub, keeping the highest sequence number per leg. Returns true.
handleReceiveFinalizedMessage.who: Circle's message transmitter, delivering an attested message. Anyone may relay Circle's attested message to the transmitter.
checks: The caller is Circle's message transmitter.
The sender is one of this contract's links on another chain, and the message comes from that link's own domain.

`READY` and a report must be finalized. An exit message is taken at any finality: entering the exit can't be undone, and it changes who controls the money, never where it can go. DLTX's keys lose their powers over this contract, and its money can then go only to the hub, which pays only the owner's withdrawal address, so a message acted on before it is final can't send money anywhere else. It is not free of market risk: the exit unwinds the positions, the short closing at once and the long as fast as its sales within the exit's price band allow, so the long stays leveraged and unhedged until it is unwound (the strategy's cash repays part of its debt first).
A leg refuses a report. The hub refuses one that does not decode as a report or names more than 16 holdings, and ignores one older than the report it holds.
Any other message reverts.

params.sourceDomain: The CCTP domain the message comes from: it must be the sending member's own.
params.sender: The address that sent the message, as 32 bytes: it must be one of this contract's links.
params.finality: The finality Circle attested the message at: `READY` and a report need finalized (2000).
params.body: The message: a tag word (`READY_MESSAGE`, `EXIT_MESSAGE` or `REPORT_MESSAGE`), and for a report the leg's figures.

handleReceiveUnfinalizedMessage.does: Receives a message from another member, attested before finality. Only an exit message is taken: it puts this contract in its exit for good, telling nobody else. `READY` and reports are refused here. Returns true.
handleReceiveUnfinalizedMessage.who: Circle's message transmitter, delivering an attested message. Anyone may relay Circle's attested message to the transmitter.
checks: The caller is Circle's message transmitter.
The sender is one of this contract's links on another chain, and the message comes from that link's own domain.
The message is exactly the exit message; anything else reverts.

params.sender: The address that sent the message, as 32 bytes: it must be one of this contract's links.
params.body: The message: only `EXIT_MESSAGE` is accepted here.

READY_MESSAGE.does: The tag of the message a member sends at creation to each member on another chain, to say it exists. No member is sent money before this message arrives.

REPORT_MESSAGE.does: The tag that opens a leg's report to its hub: its holdings, its counts of money between members, its sequence number and its observation time.

factory.does: The combination factory that created this contract. On the member code itself it reads `0x…0001`, so the code can never be initialised. A member never calls its factory after creation.

owner.does: The owner's deposit contract on this chain. The hub pays it and, in its exit, pays that contract's withdrawal address. A leg never pays it and uses it only to verify the owner's signatures.

registry.does: This chain's registry: it gives this contract its group's execution key and tells it whether the group has stopped checking in.

group.does: The execution group (0 to 15) whose key, read from the registry, operates this contract.

linkCount.does: How many other members this contract is linked to (1 to 4): on the hub, its legs; on a leg, its hub and its sister legs.

localLinks.does: Which links live on this chain, as a bitmask: bit `k` is set when link `k` is on the same chain.

configHash.does: The hash of the strategy's configuration, as the owner signed it in `CreateVault`, the same on every member.

links.does: Link `k`'s address: every other member of the strategy, in member order. On a leg, link 0 is the hub, then its sister legs; on the hub, its legs. Fixed at creation.

linkDomains.does: Link `k`'s chain, by Circle's CCTP domain number (Arbitrum 3, HyperEVM 19). Fixed at creation.

executionRevoked.does: Whether the owner has revoked the execution key on this contract (`ownerAction`). While true, the key can call nothing here.

paused.does: Whether the execution key has paused this contract (`pause`). On the long contract it blocks `supply` and `borrow`; nothing on the hub or the short contract checks it.

exiting.does: Whether this contract is in its exit. Once true it never changes back, and the execution key can call nothing here.

contracts.name: StrategyHub
contracts.title: The strategy hub
contracts.brief: A strategy's account on Arbitrum: it holds no position, funds the legs, pays you back, and pays your withdrawal address at the exit.
contracts.summary: The account of one strategy, on Arbitrum. It holds no market position and makes no market call. Your deposit contract funds it, and only it; it sends the long and short contracts their money, keeps the reports they send of what they hold, pays your deposit contract back, and computes and pays DLTX's performance fee. In an exit it first sends the long contract beside it what that contract owes and can't repay from its own USDC, so the strategy's cash repays the leveraged long before anything is sold, then pays everything else to your withdrawal address, as often as anyone asks. Each hub is a minimal copy of one code; its valuation and fee run in a fixed module, `StrategyHubFee`, whose address and code hash that code sets when it is deployed.

validateParams.does: Reverts (`BadParams`) unless the hub's parameters are within bounds: `fastFeeCapBp` at most 50, `feeBudgetBp` from 1 to 500, `feeRateBp` at most 5,000 (50 %). The combination factory calls it before it creates a hub on its chain.

params.params: The hub's parameters as the owner signed them in the configuration: an ABI-encoded `HubParams` (`fastFeeCapBp`, `feeBudgetBp`, `feeRateBp`, each in bp).

paramsType.does: The hub's parameters as the owner signs them in `CreateVault`: the typed-data struct `StrategyHub(uint16 fastFeeCapBp,uint16 feeBudgetBp,uint16 feeRateBp)`. The combination factory checks it against its pin on the hub's chain. Returns the struct's type string.

priceSources.does: The price sources of the hub's chain, as the combination factory pinned them when it created the hub, one per asset: its chain (CCTP domain), the asset, the kind (1: one Chainlink USD feed; 2: a rate feed times the base's USD feed), the feed or feeds, and `maxAge`, the oldest round accepted at the instant priced, in seconds. Their order is the order of the round hints that `value`, `preview`, `crystallize` and `payout` take.

send.does: Sends `amount` of USDC from the hub to leg `k`: on the hub's chain by a transfer the leg pulls (`receiveLocal`), otherwise by a Circle (CCTP V2) burn whose mint only that leg can complete.
send.who: The strategy group's execution key, while the owner has not revoked it and outside the exit.
send.when: Whenever a leg needs money. Pausing does not block it.
checks: The hub is not in exit (`Exiting`), the owner has not revoked the execution key (`NotAllowed`), and the caller is the group's current key (`NotExecution`).
Any USDC that reached the hub outside its own counted moves is first counted as capital: it raises the mark (`CapitalIn`).
`amount` is at most the hub's free USDC, its balance less the fees set aside (`NeedUsdc`), and is not zero (`ZeroAmount`).
Leg `k` is ready: on this chain, its code exists; on another chain, its finalized `READY` message has arrived (`NotReady`).

Across chains, Circle's minimum fee is at most 10 bp of the amount (`FeeAboveCap`). A standard transfer pays Circle's minimum only; a fast one pays at most `maxFee`, which may not exceed `fastFeeCapBp` of the amount (`FeeAboveCap`) and is raised to Circle's minimum if lower.

The burn's `maxFee` counts against the hub's fee budget: today's and yesterday's fees (UTC days), this one included, stay within `feeBudgetBp` of the hub's USDC balance before the burn (`OverFeeBudget`).

params.k: The leg, by its index among the hub's links (0 is the first leg).
params.amount: USDC, 6 decimals.
params.fast: Across chains: true for Circle's fast transfer (confirmed, with a fee), false for a standard one (finalized). No effect on the same chain.
params.maxFee: For a fast transfer, the most Circle may take, in USDC units (6 decimals). Not used for a standard transfer.

claimFee.does: Pays the fees set aside in the hub (`feeOwed`) to DLTX's fee address, as the registry of the hub's chain names it now.
claimFee.who: Anyone, in any state. The money can only go to the registry's fee address.
claimFee.when: After a fee transfer was refused and set aside.
checks: Nothing happens, without a revert, when nothing is owed, the registry names no fee address, or USDC refuses the transfer.

exitStep.does: Ends the exit's money on the hub's side, in three steps. First, each leg on the hub's chain enters its exit if it has not (a hub told by another member tells nobody, so its long contract beside it may still be running). Then, for each such leg, the hub sends it the USDC it states it owes and can't repay from its own USDC (`exitDebt`, the long contract's uncovered debt), up to the hub's free USDC, so the strategy's cash repays the leveraged long's debt before anything is sold (amendment 2d). Last, it pays everything left, less the fees set aside, to the owner's withdrawal address on the hub's chain, with DLTX's fee taken on the way. No price and no report are read.
exitStep.who: Anyone, once the hub is in exit.
exitStep.when: As often as needed: it waits for no leg, and money that arrives later is paid by a later call. Call it after the short contract's USDC reaches the hub and before the long contract's own `exitStep`.
checks: The hub is in exit (`NotExiting`).
Any USDC that reached the hub outside its own counted moves is first counted as capital (`CapitalIn`): it raises the exit's thresholds too, so it is never charged.

A leg is sent only what its own `exitDebt()` states, read with a call capped at 300,000 gas: a leg type without it, or one that fails to answer, is sent nothing. Legs on other chains are never sent anything in exit.

Each payment to a leg, and the final payout, runs on its own: one that fails (USDC refusing the leg, or the withdrawal address) is undone alone, logged (`ExitRouteFailed`, `ExitSettleFailed`), and the rest still happens. The call reverts `GasTooLow` unless it carries the gas each of them needs, so none is skipped silently.

Repaying a leg's debt needs no withdrawal address; the payout waits while none is in effect, while it names the hub or one of the strategy's own members (a member would send it back and the same cash would be counted twice), or while the hub holds no free USDC.

The fee due is the current rate on the cash the exit has paid out in all (to the owner, fees, and this call's cash) above `exitFrom`, plus `exitCheckDue`, less the exit fees already paid or forgiven, capped at this call's cash. USDC sent to a leg is not paid out, so it is charged only when it comes back and is paid.
With no fee address in the registry, the fee due is forgiven: the owner keeps it. A fee transfer refused is set aside in the hub (`FeeSetAside`) and never blocks the owner's payment.

exitRoute.does: One payment of `exitStep` to leg `k`: what the leg's `exitDebt()` states, up to the hub's free USDC, by a transfer the leg pulls (`receiveLocal`).
exitRoute.who: The hub itself only, calling itself from `exitStep` (`NotAllowed` otherwise).
checks: The caller is the hub itself.
Nothing happens when the hub has no free USDC or the leg states nothing.
`exitDebt()` is read with a staticcall capped at 300,000 gas, as one 32-byte word; a revert or a shorter answer reads as zero; less gas than the cap and 50,000 reverts `GasTooLow`.

params.k: The leg, by its index among the hub's links.

exitSettle.does: The payout of `exitStep`: everything the hub holds, less the fees set aside, to the owner's withdrawal address on the hub's chain, DLTX's exit fee taken on the way. If USDC refuses the payment, it reverts, and `exitStep` logs `ExitSettleFailed`: the payout and its fee accounting are undone, the payments to the legs stand.
exitSettle.who: The hub itself only, calling itself from `exitStep` (`NotAllowed` otherwise).
checks: The caller is the hub itself.

receiveMint.does: Completes a Circle (CCTP V2) mint bound to the hub and counts it. A burn by one of the strategy's legs is counted as money between the strategy's contracts; any other burn is accepted uncounted, and becomes capital at the hub's next count.
receiveMint.who: Anyone, in every state. Only the hub can complete a mint bound to it.
checks: The message is a burn addressed to this chain's Circle TokenMessenger, with this chain as its destination and the hub as both its caller and the mint's recipient (`BadMessage`).
Circle's message transmitter accepts it: Circle checks the attestation and the nonce (`BadMessage` if it returns false).
Exactly the amount less Circle's fee arrived (`BadMessage`).
A burn by a leg on another chain, from its own address and chain, adds to that leg's counters (`ReceivedFromLink`); any other is counted apart (`ReceivedFromOther`).

params.message: Circle's message, as the burn's source chain emitted it.

receiveReport.does: A leg on the hub's chain hands the hub its latest report directly; the hub keeps the report with the highest sequence number per leg. A leg on another chain reports by a finalized Circle message instead.
receiveReport.who: A leg of this strategy on the same chain only.
checks: The caller is a leg of this strategy on this chain (`BadMessage`).
The body is a report: the report tag, a sequence number and an observation time that fit in 64 bits, a valid encoding and at most 16 holdings (`BadMessage`).
A report whose sequence number is not higher than the one stored is ignored, without a revert.

params.body: The report: `abi.encode(REPORT_MESSAGE, seq, observedAt, observationBlock, lastMoveBlock, Holding[], sentTo[4], receivedFrom[4], feesFrom[4])`.

checkReport.does: Reverts unless `body` decodes as a leg's report with at most 16 holdings. The hub runs it on every report it receives, so a stored report can never make the value revert.

params.body: The report to check: `abi.encode(REPORT_MESSAGE, seq, observedAt, observationBlock, lastMoveBlock, Holding[], sentTo[4], receivedFrom[4], feesFrom[4])`.

reportOf.does: Leg `k`'s latest report as the hub stored it (zeros and an empty body if none has arrived).

params.k: The leg, by its index among the hub's links (0 is the first leg).

returns.seq: The report's sequence number: the highest the hub has received from that leg.
returns.observedAt: When the leg read its figures, by its own chain's clock, as a Unix time in seconds.
returns.receivedAt: When the report reached the hub, as a Unix time in seconds.
returns.body: The report itself: `abi.encode(REPORT_MESSAGE, seq, observedAt, observationBlock, lastMoveBlock, Holding[], sentTo[4], receivedFrom[4], feesFrom[4])`.

snapshotOf.does: Leg `k`'s figures as the latest `snapshot` recorded them: the ABI-encoded return of its `holdings()` (its holdings, its counters, the block, its `opCount`, whether it is tracked). Empty for a leg on another chain, or before any snapshot.

params.k: The leg, by its index among the hub's links (0 is the first leg).

fastFeeCapBp.does: The most a fast Circle transfer from the hub may pay Circle, in bp of the amount (at most 50). Fixed at creation from the owner's signed parameters.

feeBudgetBp.does: The hub's budget for Circle's fees: today's and yesterday's fees together stay within this share of the hub's USDC before each burn, in bp (1 to 500). Fixed at creation.

sequencerFeed.does: The Chainlink L2 sequencer uptime feed of the hub's chain, as the combination factory pinned it (zero on a chain with none, such as Ethereum). The snapshot and the value are refused while it reads the sequencer as down, or as restarted less than 1 hour before the instant checked.

legValueKind.does: For each of the hub's links, by index, how that leg's value is known, as the combination factory pinned it: 1 read on chain, 2 reported by DLTX (which makes the value refused, `ReportedValue`). Zero for an unused slot.

feeRateBp.does: DLTX's performance fee rate, in bp of the profit above the mark (0 to 5,000). The owner signs the starting rate in the configuration; after that only the recovery key changes it (`setFeeRate`), never above the rate signed.

signedFeeRateBp.does: The rate the owner signed in the configuration (`HubParams.feeRateBp`), in bp: the most `setFeeRate` may ever set.

lastFeeAt.does: When `crystallize` or `payout` last charged a fee above zero, as a Unix time in seconds; the hub's creation time until then. The next charge waits 1 day from it, and the profit cap counts from it. The exit's fees do not change it.

mark.does: The high-water mark, in USDC units (6 decimals), signed: the value above which profit is new. Capital in raises it, a payment to the owner lowers it, and a fee charged raises it by the profit counted less the fee, so a loss must be earned back before any new fee.

booked.does: The hub's USDC balance as its own counted moves explain it, in USDC units. Whatever the balance holds above it at the next count is capital (`CapitalIn`); a balance below it is re-based, never counted against the mark.

feeOwed.does: Fees charged whose transfer USDC refused, kept in the hub for `claimFee`, in USDC units. They are outside the value, and `send`, `payout` and `exitStep` never spend them.

exitBase.does: The mark when the exit began, raised by capital that arrives during the exit, in USDC units, signed. Recorded in `ExitSettled`; the exit's fee is computed from `exitFrom`.

exitFrom.does: The level, in USDC units, signed, above which the cash the exit has handled is charged at the current rate. It starts at the mark when the exit begins, rises with capital that arrives during the exit, and with a rate change in exit rises to the cash already handled.

exitPaid.does: What the exit has paid to the owner's withdrawal address so far, in USDC units.

exitFeePaid.does: DLTX's fee taken by the exit so far, transferred or set aside, in USDC units.

exitFeeForgiven.does: The exit's fee forgiven because the registry named no fee address when it was due (the owner kept it), in USDC units.

exitCheckDue.does: The exit's fee fixed at earlier rates by a rate change during the exit, in USDC units: the profit already handled keeps the rate it was handled at.

snapshotAt.does: When the latest snapshot was taken, as a Unix time in seconds (0: none yet).

snapshot.does: Records the instant the strategy's value starts from: for every leg on the hub's chain, its holdings, its counters and its `opCount`, read at this block. A leg on another chain is counted by its report instead.
snapshot.who: The strategy group's execution key, while the owner has not revoked it and outside the exit.
snapshot.when: Before `crystallize` or `payout`: a snapshot is usable for 10 minutes, and a leg on another chain must report 1 to 3 minutes after it.
checks: Runs only in an initialised hub, through its fee module: called on the module itself, or on the hub code, it reverts (`NotAllowed`).
The hub is not in exit (`Exiting`), the owner has not revoked the execution key (`NotAllowed`), and the caller is the group's current key (`NotExecution`).
The hub's chain has no sequencer feed, or its sequencer is up and has been for at least 1 hour (`SequencerDown`).
Every pinned price's latest round answers, is positive, and is no older than its `maxAge` (`BadRound`, `StalePrice`).
Every leg on this chain answers `holdings()` and says every change of its holdings goes through its own counted calls (`UntrackedLeg`).

crystallize.does: Charges DLTX's fee on the profit above the mark at the strategy's value now, pays it to the fee address the registry names, and raises the mark.
crystallize.who: The strategy group's execution key, while the owner has not revoked it and outside the exit.
crystallize.when: At most once a day: 1 day after `lastFeeAt` (at first, 1 day after the hub's creation).
checks: Runs only in an initialised hub, through its fee module: called on the module itself, or on the hub code, it reverts (`NotAllowed`).
The hub is not in exit (`Exiting`), the owner has not revoked the execution key (`NotAllowed`), and the caller is the group's current key (`NotExecution`).
Any USDC that reached the hub outside its own counted moves is first counted as capital: it raises the mark (`CapitalIn`).
At least 1 day has passed since `lastFeeAt` (`TooSoon`).
The value can be computed (see `value`); otherwise it reverts with the value's reason.

The profit counted is the value above the mark, capped at the mark × 50 bp for each day since `lastFeeAt` (at most 7 days); the fee is that profit × `feeRateBp` / 10,000, rounded down. A zero fee changes nothing.
With no fee address in the registry it charges nothing and emits `FeeDeferred`.
The hub's free USDC covers the fee (`NeedUsdc`). A fee transfer USDC refuses is set aside in the hub (`FeeSetAside`).
The mark rises by the profit counted less the fee, and `lastFeeAt` becomes now.

params.rounds: One Chainlink round id per feed, in the order of `priceSources()` (one for a single feed; two for a composite, the rate's then the base's): the round in effect at the instant priced. The hub checks each round; it never searches for one.

payout.does: Pays `amount` of USDC to the owner's deposit contract on the hub's chain, and lowers the mark by as much. It charges DLTX's fee first when it can, and pays anyway when it can't.
payout.who: The strategy group's execution key, while the owner has not revoked it and outside the exit. The money can only go to the owner's deposit contract.
checks: Runs only in an initialised hub, through its fee module: called on the module itself, or on the hub code, it reverts (`NotAllowed`).
The hub is not in exit (`Exiting`), the owner has not revoked the execution key (`NotAllowed`), and the caller is the group's current key (`NotExecution`).
Any USDC that reached the hub outside its own counted moves is first counted as capital: it raises the mark (`CapitalIn`).

If 1 day has passed since `lastFeeAt`, the value can be computed and the hub's free USDC covers both `amount` and the fee, the fee is charged first as `crystallize` charges it. Otherwise it emits `FeeDeferred` with the reason, and the profit stays above the mark for a later charge.
`amount` is at most the hub's free USDC, its balance less the fees set aside (`NeedUsdc`).

params.amount: USDC to pay, 6 decimals.
params.rounds: One Chainlink round id per feed, in the order of `priceSources()` (one for a single feed; two for a composite, the rate's then the base's): the round in effect at the instant priced. The hub checks each round; it never searches for one.

setFeeRate.does: Sets the strategy's performance fee rate, never above the rate the owner signed: lower at any time, back up to the signed rate outside the exit. The new rate applies to every profit not yet charged; the change itself charges nothing.
setFeeRate.who: The recovery key of the hub chain's registry only, in any state, the exit included (in exit, only a lowering). The owner cannot change the rate.
checks: Runs only in an initialised hub, through its fee module: called on the module itself, or on the hub code, it reverts (`NotAllowed`).
The caller is the registry's recovery key (`NotAllowed`).
`newBp` is at most the rate the owner signed (`signedFeeRateBp`), and in exit at most the current rate (`BadRate`).
Any USDC that reached the hub outside its own counted moves is first counted as capital (`CapitalIn`).
In exit, the profit the exit already handled keeps the old rate (fixed into `exitCheckDue`); every later dollar takes the new, lower one.

params.newBp: The new rate, in bp of the profit above the mark (0 to the signed rate).

value.does: The strategy's value now, in USDC units (6 decimals), signed: the hub's free USDC, plus every leg's holdings at their prices, plus the money in transit between the strategy's contracts (for each pair, what one sent the other less what the other recorded receiving from it). The legs beside the hub count by the snapshot, a leg on another chain by its report, every asset at the Chainlink round in effect at that report's observation (the snapshot's time when no leg is elsewhere). When the value can't be computed, it returns the reason instead.
checks: A snapshot exists and is at most 10 minutes old (`NoSnapshot`).
Every leg's value is read on chain (`ReportedValue`), and at most one leg is on another chain (`TooManyRemote`).
Each leg on the hub's chain is unchanged since the snapshot: the same `opCount`, every holding other than USD within 1 bp, none appeared or vanished (`PositionMoved`).

The leg on another chain has a report at most 10 minutes old (`StaleReport`), not more than 1 minute ahead of the hub's clock (`FutureReport`), observed 1 to 3 minutes after the snapshot (`SnapshotIncomplete`), and at least 3 blocks after its last move between HyperEVM and HyperCore (`MoveSettling`).
The hub's chain has no sequencer feed, or its sequencer is up now and has been since at least 1 hour before the instant priced (`SequencerDown`).

Every holding's asset has a pinned price (`UnknownAsset`); each round hint is the round in effect at the instant, in its feed's latest phase, positive and no older than `maxAge` (`BadRound`, `StalePrice`).
No holding, price or counter is beyond 2^120 (`ValueOutOfRange`).

returns.ok: Whether the value could be computed.
returns.v: The value, in USDC units (6 decimals), signed; 0 when refused.
returns.why: When refused, the reason: an error's selector in the first 4 bytes (`NoSnapshot`, `StaleReport`, `PositionMoved` and the others above); zero otherwise.

errors.NoUsdc: The hub is on a chain outside its USDC table (Ethereum, Avalanche, OP Mainnet, Arbitrum, Base, Polygon, HyperEVM).

contracts.name: LongVault
contracts.title: The long contract
contracts.brief: A strategy's Aave V3 position on Arbitrum: WETH supplied, USDC borrowed, within the limits you signed.
contracts.summary: The leg that holds a strategy's long, on Arbitrum: WETH supplied to Aave V3 and USDC borrowed against it. DLTX's execution key operates it within limits fixed when the strategy is created (the health floor, the price bound, the daily loss budget, the fast-bridge fee cap); it swaps only in one pinned Uniswap pool, and repays with collateral only through DLTX's repay-with-collateral contract. It sends money only to the strategy's other contracts. In an exit it unwinds in independent parts, every sale held at the margin to 50 bp of Aave's oracle (so moving the pool first gains a caller nothing beyond that), and sends everything to its hub. Its exit runs in a fixed module, `LongVaultExit`. It can claim the incentives Aave and Merkl pay it, and sells the pinned reward (ARB) for USDC on one pinned pool, within 1 % of Chainlink's price.

legInfo.does: Declares what kind of leg this is: its type, the roles it can play and how its value is known. The combination factory checks the roles and the value kind against its own pins when it is deployed on this chain.

returns.roles: One bit per role the leg can play: 1, the long only.
returns.valueKind: 1: the leg's value is read on chain from its own balances, never reported by DLTX.

paramsType.does: This leg's parameters as the owner signs them in `CreateVault`: the typed-data struct `AaveV3Leg(address pool,address oracle,address weth,address usdc,address swapPool,address receiver,uint64 healthFloor,uint16 oracleBoundBp,uint16 dailyLossBp,uint16 fastFeeCapBp)`. The combination factory checks it against its pin on Arbitrum. Returns the struct's type string.

validateParams.does: Checks a configuration's parameters for this leg and reverts unless they are acceptable. The combination factory calls it before creating the strategy's contracts on this chain, so a strategy the owner signed with other protocols or numbers outside these bounds is never created.
checks: The six addresses are exactly the ones this code is pinned to on Arbitrum: Aave V3's pool `0x794a61358D6845594F94dc1DB02A252b5b4814aD`, Aave's price oracle `0xb56c2F0B653B2e0b10C9b928C8580Ac5Df02C7C7`, WETH `0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1`, USDC `0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831`, the Uniswap V3 WETH/USDC pool at the 0.05% fee `0xC6962004f452bE9203591991D15f6b388e09E8D0`, and DLTX's repay-with-collateral contract, already deployed on Arbitrum and used by DLTX's current product (Contract addresses lists it once the strategy contracts are deployed, whose verified code names it).
The health floor is between 1.05 and 3.0 (Aave's scale, 18 decimals).
The oracle bound is between 30 and 500 bp.
The daily loss budget is at most 500 bp.
The fast-transfer fee cap is at most 50 bp.

params.params: The leg's parameters, ABI-encoded as `LongParams`: the pool, the oracle, WETH, USDC, the swap pool and the repay-with-collateral contract, then the health floor (18 decimals, 1e18 = 1.0), the oracle bound, the daily loss budget and the fast-transfer fee cap (each in bp).

swap.does: Swaps WETH for USDC, or USDC for WETH, on the pinned Uniswap V3 pool, paid to this contract, and returns the amount received. What the swap loses against Aave's oracle is charged to the 24-hour loss budget. Counted in `opCount`.

swap.when: Outside the exit, paused or not.

The amount in is not zero.
The minimum out is raised to at least the amount in at Aave's oracle price less the oracle bound; a tighter one asked for is kept.
The swap is on the pool itself, exact input, no router; the contract pays the pool only in its callback, during this call.
It receives at least the minimum, or the call reverts.
The loss against the oracle, added to what the budget has already counted today and yesterday, is at most the daily loss budget of the position's equity read before the swap.

repayWithCollateral.does: Repays USDC debt with the position's own collateral in one transaction, through DLTX's pinned repay-with-collateral contract: a flash loan of the USDC repays the debt, and the collateral it frees is sold to pay the loan back. What actually moved is measured afterwards, and what it lost against Aave's oracle is charged to the 24-hour loss budget. Counted in `opCount`.

repayWithCollateral.when: Outside the exit, paused or not.

The debt to repay is not zero.
The most collateral it may spend is at most the debt's value at Aave's oracle plus the oracle bound, which covers the swap pool's fee and Aave's flash-loan premium.
The repay-with-collateral contract is approved for exactly that collateral (aWETH), and the approval is reset to zero afterwards.
Measured afterwards: the collateral that left (less any WETH handed back) against the debt repaid (plus any USDC handed back) loses at most the oracle bound of the collateral's value.
That loss fits in the daily loss budget of the position's equity read before the call.
Aave's health factor afterwards is not lower than before.

Outside the exit, the health factor afterwards is at least the contract's health floor.

send.when: Outside the exit, paused or not, once the receiving contract has announced itself.
checks: The contract is not in exit, the owner has not revoked the execution key, and the caller is the group's current execution key.
The amount is not zero.
The receiving contract is ready: on this chain its code is deployed; on another chain its finalized `READY` message has arrived.
Across chains: Circle's minimum fee for the amount, read in the call, is at most 10 bp of it, or the call reverts rather than paying it.

A standard transfer (finalized) pays Circle's minimum fee only. A fast transfer (confirmed) pays up to `maxFee`, at most the fast-transfer fee cap of the amount, and raised to Circle's minimum if lower.

lossInWindow.does: The losses the 24-hour budget counts right now, in USD with 8 decimals (Aave's oracle base): today's bucket and yesterday's, both in full. Any 24 hours fall within two consecutive UTC days, so no 24 hours can lose more than the budget.

claimMerkl.who: The strategy group's execution key outside the exit, unless the owner revoked it on this contract; anyone in the exit (the owner, a keeper, the escape hatch).
claimMerkl.when: In every state but before the exit only by the key; paused or not.
checks: Outside the exit: the owner has not revoked the execution key, and the caller is the group's current execution key.
The distributor is fixed in the code, and every claim names this contract as the user.

params.amounts: Each token's cumulative amount in Merkl's tree, in its smallest unit.
params.proofs: Each claim's Merkle proof, from Merkl's API, for the distributor's current root.

The sale must return at least the reward's value at Chainlink's ARB / USD less 1 %; what it loses against that value is counted in the 24-hour loss budget outside the exit, but never refused by it (the sale is one way: nothing buys ARB back). Counted in `opCount`.
swapReward.who: The strategy group's execution key outside the exit, unless the owner revoked it on this contract; anyone in the exit (the owner, a keeper, the escape hatch).
swapReward.when: In every state but before the exit only by the key; paused or not.

aArbARB is not enabled as collateral on this contract (`rewardCollateralOff` first).
A withdrawal of aArbARB leaves Aave's health factor no lower than before.
Chainlink's ARB / USD answered within the last 25 hours, and Arbitrum's sequencer has been up for at least an hour.
The minimum out is raised to at least the amount's value at the feed less 1 %; a tighter one asked for is kept, and the pool must pay at least it.
Only ARB is sold, only to the pinned pool, paid only in its callback during this call.

In exit only: the sale fills only at pool prices no worse than the feed's ARB price in USDC less 50 bp, so it may fill in part (the rest waits for a later call), and the minimum out and the 1 % floor apply to what was sold; the pool already below that price, it sells nothing (`PoolOffOracle`).

params.minOut: The least USDC to accept, in its smallest unit (6 decimals); raised to the contract's own bound when lower.

rewardCollateralOff.who: The strategy group's execution key outside the exit, unless the owner revoked it on this contract; anyone in the exit (the owner, a keeper, the escape hatch).
rewardCollateralOff.when: In every state but before the exit only by the key; paused or not.
checks: Outside the exit: the owner has not revoked the execution key, and the caller is the group's current execution key.
Aave refuses it below a health factor of 1; outside the exit, the health factor must stay at or above the health floor.

rewardPins.does: The rewards path's pins, fixed in the code: its two sources (Aave's RewardsController, Merkl's distributor), the reward token (ARB) and its Aave token (aArbARB), the pool it is sold on, the Chainlink feed that bounds the sale, the feed's maximum age (25 hours) and the bound (100 bp).

returns.pool: The Uniswap V3 ARB/USDC pool, fee 0.30 %.
returns.maxAge: The oldest feed answer accepted, in seconds.
returns.boundBp: The most a sale may lose against the feed, in basis points.

exitStep.does: Unwinds the Aave position and sends the proceeds to the hub, which pays the owner's withdrawal address. Each part runs on its own so that one that fails (a paused reserve, no flash liquidity, a pool away from the oracle, a stale price) logs `ExitPartFailed` and the others still run. First, when the contract holds the pinned reward (ARB or aArbARB, at least 0.01) or has aArbARB on as collateral, the reward parts: turn aArbARB's collateral off, then sell the reward for USDC, each with its own gas cap. Then: repay the debt with the USDC held (including what the hub sent it in exit), then with the USDC supplied (aUSDC), then with collateral through the repay-with-collateral contract or, if that fails, by withdrawing what Aave lets go, selling and repaying; once the debt is zero, withdraw the WETH and the USDC supplied, each as far as Aave holds it; sell the WETH held; send the USDC held to the hub, less what still repays a debt. A sale may fill in part: what the price band does not let it sell waits for a later call. Counted in `opCount`.
exitStep.who: Anyone, as often as needed: it takes no recipient and pays only the hub.
exitStep.when: Only in exit, until nothing is left.
checks: Called on a strategy's own contract, never on the module or the leg code directly.
The contract is in exit.

With reward work, the call reverts `GasTooLow` unless it carries enough gas for both reward parts' caps and the position's parts: the reward is never skipped silently. Whether there is reward work is read with capped calls; a reward token that fails to answer counts as none.

Every WETH sale in exit fills only at pool prices no worse than Aave's oracle less 50 bp (less when the owner signed an oracle bound under 55 bp: the bound less the pool's 0.05 % fee), so a caller who moves the pool first can't make it sell cheaper; the pool already below that price, the part sells nothing (`PoolOffOracle`). Its average must still reach the oracle less the oracle bound, on what it sold.

The repay with collateral, whose sale runs inside the repay-with-collateral contract, reads the pool's price before (`PoolOffOracle`) and after (`BandCrossed`: the chunk was too big for the band, nothing is repaid); `debtChunk` sizes it. With `debtChunk` 0 a debt larger than the band holds goes to the fallback, which makes progress while the health factor is above 1 and AAVE has WETH to lend out; otherwise a smaller `debtChunk` on the repay with collateral is the way forward.

The fallback withdraws at most the collateral Aave lets go (the liquidation-weighted collateral above the debt, less 1 %, as if the WETH withdrawn counted in full, so never more than Aave allows whatever other collateral is held) and what the reserve holds, sells what the band allows, supplies the rest back, repays, and leaves the health factor no lower than before.
The reward sale in exit fills only at prices no worse than Chainlink's ARB / USD less 50 bp, its average at least that value less 1 % on what it sold. Outside the exit the key's sales are unchanged.
While a debt stands, the USDC sent to the hub leaves on the contract its debt and a small headroom (10 bp and 1 USDC), so USDC the hub sent to repay the debt never goes back.
A reward part keeps at most 256 bytes of its revert data in `ExitPartFailed`. The daily loss budget does not apply in exit.

The payment to the hub never reverts: on the same chain it is a transfer whose failure is ignored; across chains a standard Circle burn bound to the hub, skipped while Circle's minimum fee is above 10 bp or Circle refuses it.

params.debtChunk: The most debt to repay with collateral in this call, in USDC's smallest unit (6 decimals); 0 repays all of it, or, when that is more than the price band holds, leaves it to the fallback.
params.wethChunk: The most WETH to sell in this call, in wei (18 decimals); 0 sells all of it, as far as the price band allows.

exitPart.does: Runs one part of `exitStep`, so that it can fail on its own: 1 repays with the USDC held; 2 repays with the aUSDC held (Aave's `repayWithATokens`); 3 repays with collateral through the repay-with-collateral contract, the pool's price read before and after; 4 repays by withdrawing what Aave lets go, selling it within the band, supplying back what was not sold and repaying; 5 withdraws the WETH supplied once the debt is zero, as far as the reserve holds it; 10 does the same for the USDC supplied; 6 sells the WETH held for USDC within the band; 7 sends the USDC held to the hub, less the debt and its headroom while one stands; 8 sells the pinned reward held (ARB, and aArbARB withdrawn), nothing under 0.01; 9 turns aArbARB's collateral off when it is on.
exitPart.who: This contract only, calling itself from `exitStep`.
checks: The caller is this contract itself.
Parts 1 to 4 do nothing once the debt is zero, and parts 5 and 10 nothing while there is debt.

Parts 3 and 4 spend at most the collateral bound for the chunk of debt (its value at Aave's oracle plus the oracle bound), and never more aWETH than is held; part 4 at most the liquidation-weighted collateral above the debt, less 1 %, and what the WETH reserve holds.
Parts 3, 4 and 6 refuse a pool already at or below the band's limit (`PoolOffOracle`); part 3 refuses a repay that left the pool below it (`BandCrossed`).
Part 4 reverts if the health factor ends lower than before, or if Aave refuses to take back the unsold WETH.

params.part: Which part to run, 1 to 10 (9 and 8 run first, when there is reward work; 10 after 5).
params.arg: For parts 3 and 4, the most debt to repay (USDC, 6 decimals; 0 all of it); for part 6, the most WETH to sell (18 decimals; 0 all of it); unused by the other parts.

exitDebt.does: In exit, the USDC this contract owes and can't repay from its own USDC and aUSDC, plus 10 bp of it and 1 USDC of headroom for the interest that accrues before its next `exitStep`; zero when it owes nothing uncovered, and zero outside the exit. The hub beside it sends it at most this, before paying the owner (amendment 2d). In USDC, 6 decimals. Zero, too, while the position is insolvent: its WETH at Aave's oracle worth less than its debt (USDC at $1), read without Aave's loop over every reserve, so no stranger's dust can push the hub's capped read out of gas. That debt is Aave's liquidators' to write off, never the owner's cash to repay.

checks: The message is a burn to this chain, addressed to this chain's Circle TokenMessenger, with this contract as both the mint's recipient and the only caller allowed to complete it.
Circle's transmitter checks the attestation and that the message is used once.
Exactly the amount burned less Circle's fee arrived.

report.who: Anyone: it reports to the hub only.
checks: Every figure is read in this one block.
On the hub's chain the hub takes it directly; on another chain it goes as a Circle message at finalized finality, and the call reverts if Circle refuses it.

holdings.does: The report's figures as a view, so that a hub on the same chain can read them without a message. The holdings are two: `ETH`, the aWETH and WETH held, and `USD`, the USDC and aUSDC held less the variable USDC debt, both signed and in 18 decimals.

returns.2: What this contract has sent to each other contract of the strategy, gross, by link (0 the hub).
returns.3: What it has received from each other contract of the strategy, gross, by link.

returns.6: How many counted calls it has made (`opCount`): the hub sees a move between two readings.

errors.BadAsset: `withdraw` was asked for a token other than WETH or USDC.
errors.BelowHealthFloor: A borrow, a withdrawal or an e-mode change would leave Aave's health factor below the health floor.
errors.HealthFell: A repay with collateral, or the exit's repay by sale, left Aave's health factor lower than before.
errors.AboveBound: A repay with collateral offered more collateral than the oracle bound allows for the debt, or lost more than the oracle bound of the collateral's value.
errors.OverBudget: A sale's loss against Aave's oracle, or a Circle fee on `send`, would take the losses counted today and yesterday above the daily loss budget of the position's equity. A reward sale is counted in the budget but never refused by it.
errors.SwapShort: The pool paid less than the minimum out, raised to the oracle bound.
errors.BadParams: A configuration names protocols other than the pinned ones, or numbers outside this leg's bounds.

contracts.name: ShortVault
contracts.title: The short contract
contracts.brief: A strategy's Hyperliquid account, on HyperEVM: the short is held in the contract's own name.
contracts.summary: The leg that holds a strategy's short, on HyperEVM: the contract is the Hyperliquid account itself. A trading agent trades it: Hyperliquid lets an agent trade and change some account settings, never withdraw to an outside address, so it can still lose the account's money by trading; DLTX's execution key moves its margin, reduces or closes the position with reduce-only orders within the order bound, and sends money only to the strategy's other contracts. You can replace the agent with an inert one at once. In an exit it closes everything at oracle prices and burns its USDC to its hub over Circle's bridge. Its exit runs in a fixed module, `ShortVaultExit`.

returns.roles: The roles this leg may take, one bit each: 3, both long (1) and short (2).
returns.valueKind: How its value is known: 1, read on chain (the hub may value it from figures the contract reads itself).

paramsType.does: This leg's parameters as the owner signs them in `CreateVault`: the typed-data struct `HyperCoreLeg(uint32 perp,bytes32 asset,uint16 orderBoundBp,uint16 fastFeeCapBp,uint16 feeBudgetBp)`, named by the leg type, which may play either role. The combination factory checks it against its pin on HyperEVM. Returns the struct's type string.

The asset is named and is not USD.
The order bound is 30 to 1,000 bp.
The fast-fee cap is at most 50 bp.
The fee budget is 1 to 500 bp.

receive.does: Accepts HYPE on HyperEVM, and only from Hyperliquid's HYPE system address: HYPE coming back from this account's HyperCore balance.

toMargin.who: The execution key, while not revoked.
checks: The caller is the group's execution key in the registry, the owner has not revoked it, and the contract is not in exit.

fromMargin.does: Brings USDC back from HyperCore to this contract on HyperEVM, in two HyperCore actions: perp margin to spot, then spot to HyperEVM. HyperCore carries them out after the transaction; one it refuses does not revert this call.

fromMargin.when: Outside the exit. The second action's fee is paid in HYPE from the account's spot balance, so it needs a little HYPE there (`topUpHype`). The account's first outgoing USDC transfer also pays about 1 USDC from spot on top of the amount; on a first call with no other USDC on spot, HyperCore drops the second action silently and the amount stays on spot. `prime` pays that fee first.

prime.does: Pays the account's first-transfer fee, about 1 USDC in USDC, which HyperCore charges on an account's first outgoing USDC transfer and which `fromMargin` cannot pay on a fresh account: it moves 1.2 USDC of perp margin to spot, then sends 0.05 USDC from spot to this contract on HyperEVM, so the amount and the fee fit. About 0.145 USDC stays on spot. In unified mode the first action may do nothing; spot is then the whole balance and pays. HyperCore carries both out after the transaction; one it refuses does not revert this call. Calling it again is harmless: the money stays in the account. Counted in `opCount`.
prime.who: The execution key, while not revoked.
prime.when: Outside the exit, once at custody creation, with HYPE on the account's spot for the second action's fee.
checks: The caller is the group's execution key in the registry, the owner has not revoked it, and the contract is not in exit.
